rules.title: The + adjective for a group: the rich, the French
rules.short_explanation: Use the + an adjective to mean a whole group of people: the rich, the elderly, the unemployed. Use the + a nationality ending in -ch, -sh, -ese or -ss to mean the people of that country: the French, the Swiss, the Chinese.
rules.tts_text: The rich and the French: the adjective or nationality means a whole group.
rules.mnemonic: The + adjective = a crowd of people.

rules.title: Such a, what a, quite a: the article comes after the word
rules.short_explanation: After such, what, quite, rather and half, a singular countable noun takes a or an after that word: such a day, what a view, half an hour. With plural or uncountable nouns there is no article: such nice people, what beautiful weather.
rules.tts_text: Say: such a long day, what a view, half an hour.
rules.mnemonic: Such, what, quite: the article comes after, one thing only.

examples.text: We had such a long day at the warehouse.
